about: Own-words reads from the daily research task (ADMIS, Rabobank, Czapp and the news feed). fund_score: -1 bearish to +1 bullish, a judgement on the fundamental news only.

cotton.fundamental: Still no fresh supply news: harvest reports keep describing uneven US yields, and Dec is in delivery near 75.8, so the live read is Mar/May/Jul. The broad risk-off move in equities today is a demand-side headwind for a fund-driven market; high-grade certs remain the thing to watch for longs.
events: Mixed US cotton yields after weather extremes (Farm Progress)
Wall Street AI-led rout, VIX near 35 (AP, Yahoo Finance)

sugar.fundamental: Brazil is still the driver: the real weakened again (USD/BRL near 5.95), keeping Centre-South export parity cheap, and Mar has slipped through the 17.13-17.14 support band to around 17.07. Talk of a better supply outlook adds to it; the weak French beet crop is only a marginal offset for whites.
events: Mar raw sugar breaks below 17.13 as the real slides (Barchart, Yahoo Finance)
Improved supply outlook weighs on sugar (Barchart)
Tereos cuts outlook on poor French beet crop (Investing.com)

coffee.fundamental: Arabica gave back about 3% on talk of stronger Brazilian exports and a weaker real, which encourages farmer selling. There is still no new ICE certified-stock or Antwerp figure, so the support from thin exchange stocks is unchanged; if Brazil shipments do pick up, that would ease deliverability concerns over the next couple of months.
events: Outlook for stronger Brazil exports weighs on arabica (Barchart)
Real weakens toward 5.95 per dollar (Yahoo Finance)

cocoa.fundamental: Cocoa firmed about 1.5-2% as supply risks came back into focus: an El Nino warning for the coming West African seasons and the risk that rains and congestion slow Ivorian port arrivals. Rising ICE stocks still cap rallies, and European buyers paying up ahead of EU deforestation rules supports physical premiums.
events: El Nino risk hits the cocoa output outlook (ADMIS)
European cocoa premiums firm before deforestation rules (Bloomberg)
